skill.name: agentix-ceo
skill.description: Orchestrate Agentix teams by configuring roles, creating tasks, launching workers, and monitoring progress through SaaS or self-hosted APIs.
skill.summary: Coordinate Agentix roles, tasks, workers, playbooks, and team progress.
skill.author: agentix-cloud

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, while Agentix endpoint references are intentional network behavior. The skill collects high-value credentials, transmits them to Agentix, and follows remotely fetched playbooks. Unauthenticated self-hosting and autonomous worker mode add further operational risk.

remediation.issue: The workflow collects Anthropic and GitHub credentials for transfer to Agentix.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent that names the destination, accept only scoped short-lived tokens, and support secret-manager references instead of raw credentials.

remediation.issue: Agentix credentials are stored in a plaintext hidden file and loaded silently.
remediation.suggestion: Use the operating system credential store. If a file is unavoidable, require confirmation and enforce owner-only permissions before writing.

remediation.issue: Remote playbook text controls agent policies and operating mode.
remediation.suggestion: Treat playbooks as untrusted data, validate allowed directives, reject instruction overrides, and require approval before privileged actions.

remediation.issue: The self-hosted API is documented as unauthenticated and open on the local network.
remediation.suggestion: Require authentication, bind to loopback by default, and document secure network exposure with transport encryption.

remediation.issue: Autopilot has no documented limits for concurrency, spending, or repository changes.
remediation.suggestion: Add worker, cost, and time limits. Require approval for merges, credential updates, role deletion, and destructive task changes.

semantic_findings.description: The self-hosted path states that its API has no authentication and is open on the local network. Other local-network users could control teams and workers.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented mode grants full autonomy and continuous looping without defining concurrency, cost, or merge limits.

content.value_statement: Coordinating several AI workers can make roles, tasks, and progress difficult to track. This skill manages Agentix teams through a structured API workflow.
actual_capabilities: Configure an Agentix SaaS endpoint or a user-selected self-hosted endpoint.
Register SaaS users, poll confirmation status, and persist returned Agentix credentials.
Read and update team playbooks, roles, tasks, and API keys.
Launch or resume workers for assigned tasks and inspect their status.
Monitor team summaries, task progress, active workers, and recent events.
Configure repository integration and an Anthropic key for worker execution.
limitations: The skill requires network access to Agentix SaaS or a reachable self-hosted instance.
Worker execution requires a user-provided Anthropic API key and may incur external costs.
Credentials are documented as plaintext values in a hidden home file.
Self-hosted mode assumes an unauthenticated API, which is unsafe on untrusted networks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Create specialist roles, assign approved tasks, launch workers, and monitor delivery from one team view.

use_cases.title: Run a Solo Project Team
use_cases.description: Delegate implementation and review tasks to temporary workers while keeping project progress visible.

use_cases.title: Operate a Self-Hosted Team
use_cases.description: Connect to an internal Agentix instance, configure a stable team, and monitor worker activity.

prompt_templates.title: Review Team Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the Agentix team summary, active workers, and recent events. Do not create or update anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Roles and Assignments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current roles and ready tasks. Recommend missing roles and task assignments. Ask for approval before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Launch Approved Workers
prompt_templates.prompt: In supervised mode, launch workers for the approved ready tasks. Report each worker identifier, assigned role, and task status.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Guarded Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the approved backlog with at most three concurrent workers. Stop before merges or credential changes and request approval.

output_examples.input: Show my current team status without changing anything.
output: Team summary with its goal, current playbook mode, and configured roles.
Active worker list with assigned tasks and current statuses.
Recent event summary highlighting completed, failed, and blocked work.

output_examples.input: Launch one backend worker for the approved authentication task.
output_examples.output: The approved task is assigned to the existing backend role. One worker is launched, and its current status is reported.

output_examples.input: Recommend a guarded plan for the ready backlog.
output_examples.output: The response groups tasks by role, identifies dependencies, proposes a concurrency limit, and marks merges or credential changes for approval.

best_practices: Use supervised mode until roles, permissions, budgets, and approval gates are verified.
Provide scoped, short-lived credentials and confirm the destination before any secret transfer.
Set explicit worker, cost, and time limits before launching multiple tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not enable autopilot without concurrency, spending, and merge controls.
Do not expose an unauthenticated self-hosted API beyond a trusted local interface.
Do not place broad GitHub or Anthropic credentials in team configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill require Agentix SaaS?
faq.answer: No. It supports a self-hosted endpoint, but the documented self-hosted path lacks authentication and requires network safeguards.

faq.question: Is an Anthropic API key required?
faq.answer: Yes, worker execution requires an Anthropic API key. Team inspection and configuration may work before workers are launched.

faq.question: Where are Agentix credentials stored?
faq.answer: The skill documents a hidden plaintext file in the user home directory. Protect it with strict permissions or use a credential store.

faq.question: Can the skill create roles and tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list, create, update, and delete roles or tasks through the Agentix API.

faq.question: What is the difference between supervised and autopilot modes?
faq.answer: Supervised mode requires approval for new work. Autopilot permits continuous planning, worker launches, reviews, and merges.

faq.question: How can I keep control of repository changes?
faq.answer: Use supervised mode, restrict token permissions, and require approval before merges, role deletion, or credential updates.
